title: Build a Mini Redis: RESP Protocol & an Event-Loop Server
summary:
Build a single-threaded, event-loop key-value server that real Redis clients could talk to. You write a **RESP2 serializer** and an **incremental parser** that copes with frames split at any TCP byte boundary and with **pipelined** requests, a **`node:net` server** (port 0, the OS picks), the core string commands (`PING ECHO GET SET[EX|PX|NX|XX] DEL EXISTS INCR EXPIRE TTL`) with Redis's exact replies and error strings, **lazy + active expiry** on an injected clock, and **graceful shutdown**.

Interview payoff: you can explain why one thread with an event loop (epoll/kqueue) handles 100k connections, why TCP is a byte stream and not a message stream, how pipelining amortises round trips, how Redis reclaims expired keys nobody reads, why `SET NX PX` is the building block of a lock, and what draining a server looks like during a deploy.

milestones.name: M1: RESP serializer
milestones.description: `encode` for simple strings, errors, integers (incl. bigint), bulk strings (byte lengths, null) and arrays (nested, null).

milestones.name: M2: Incremental RESP parser
milestones.description: `RespParser.push(chunk)` returns all complete frames and buffers the rest; works for every split point and byte-by-byte; throws `ProtocolError` on malformed input.

milestones.name: M3: Commands
milestones.description: `execute(args)` for PING, ECHO, GET, SET with EX/PX/NX/XX validation, DEL, EXISTS, INCR with int64 overflow detection — exact Redis error strings, case-insensitive names.

milestones.name: M4: Expiry
milestones.description: TTLs on the injected clock: lazy expiry on every read path, `TTL`/`PTTL`/`EXPIRE` semantics (SET clears TTL, INCR keeps it, EXPIRE ≤ 0 deletes), and `activeExpireCycle(maxChecks)` reclaiming keys nobody reads.

milestones.name: M5: Event-loop TCP server
milestones.description: `listen(0)` returns the port; per-connection parser; pipelined in-order replies; split frames; many concurrent clients; protocol errors close only that connection; graceful `close()` that flushes replies, ends idle clients and refuses new connections.
